newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
PAKISTAN STICKS WITH KASHMIR ROW

Pakistan seems firm on raking up Kashmir as the core issue at the foreign secretary-level talks in New Delhi. Any Indian attempt to widen the ambit of dialogue may be resisted by the Pakistani delegation. On his arrival in New Delhi, the Pakistani foreign secretary pointed out the urgent need to address all outstanding issues, including the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir.
The Hindustan Times
OPPOSITION PLANS CONDITIONS FOR PRESIDENTIAL POLL

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is thinking of setting its own terms for consensus over the next president of the country. In return, the party proposed to insist on accommodating its nominee for the vice-president's post. The BJP, with 1.13 million votes as against the Congress's 1.11 million in the electoral college for the presidential elections, began to flex its muscles recently when its vice-president commented that their role in these elections would be important.
The Times of India
FARMERS SET TO GET MORE FOR THEIR WHEAT

In a bid to maximise wheat procurement in the current harvest season, the government will soon announce an advance bonus to farmers over and above the existing minimum support price. In effect, this would raise the wheat procurement price by about 100 rupees a quintal. However, the government was not averse to importing wheat to bolster its stocks and maintain price stability.
The Economic Times
STATE BANK SEEKING TO FINANCE FRIENDLY TAKEOVERS

The State Bank of India (SBI) is revamping the loan portfolio of its foreign branches. It will sharply cut its ethnic loans and focus only on loans linked specifically to imports and exports. It is also reassessing its loan exposure in companies affected by progressive import duty cuts. Its risk management cell is examining lending portfolio in duty sensitive industries including polyester, steel, computer hardware and capital goods. SBI is also keen to fund non-hostile and non-speculative takeovers of small firms by large corporates.
AIRCRAFT SHOULD HAVE ANTI-COLLISION DEVICES

The director-general of civil aviation (DGCA) has called a meeting on April 16 of over 40 international airlines and private operators in which new air safety norms will be announced. The DGCA will make it mandatory for all players to install airborne collision avoidance systems (ACAS) in their carriers. These guidelines would apply to airlines that operate from India as well as those flying over Indian airspace.
PAKISTAN REPORT FAVOURS TRADING WITH INDIA

A confidential report prepared by Pakistan's Commerce Ministry said the economic benefits of liberalising bilateral trade with India outweighed the costs. These findings formed the basis for the secretary-level talks, a prelude to the meeting of the foreign ministers of both countries. Consumers and the Pakistan government would benefit significantly if both governments implemented policy measures to liberalise trade.
LIMIT ON FLOOR AREA OF URBAN HOLDINGS LIKELY TO BE DOUBLED

The government has proposed a 100 percent increase in the upper limit on the floor area for land holdings and a levy of shelter tax on commercial buildings. These formed part of the exercise to amend the Urban Land Ceiling and Regulation Act. The compensation package for land owners was also set to change.
Financial Express
GOVERNMENT TO STRESS CONSOLIDATION, NOT CHANGE

Virtually all the existing schemes are going to figure in the new five-year export-import policy. The policy, effective from April 1, 1997, is unlikely to spring any surprises for the exporting community. Sources said the accent would be on consolidation of all existing schemes by rationalising procedures. Sources said only a few items were proposed to be shifted from the restricted to the freely importable and special import licence lists in accordance with the government's commitment to the WTO.

APEX BANK HIKES GILT PRICES, SIGNALLING INTEREST RATE FALL The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has signalled a fall in interest rates at the long end of the market by jacking up the price of the 14 percent nine-year paper maturing in 2005 by 0.24 rupees. This was one of the steepest hikes to be effected by the apex bank for a long-term security. Foreign banks, usually shy of picking up long-term papers, were making a beeline for long dated securities, primarily for trading purposes.
GOVERNMENT BANKS SET TO MEET PRIORITY LENDING TARGET

After five years, government banks will meet the priority sector lending target -- 40 percent of net bank credit -- in 1996/97 (April-March). In September 1996, such lending was pegged at 40.75 percent but jumped to 41.12 percent in December 1996.
Business Standard
SWISS TELECOM TO OFFER ROAMING FACILITY

Swiss Telecom will soon offer Indian cellular telecommunications operators access to its international roaming facilities and clearing house. Named Ubicom, the offer will also market the international roaming service to cellular service group special mobile (GSM) and PCS-1900, both digital standard providers in North America. Cellular networks in India operate on the GSM standard. The service will offer seamless roaming agreements with 113 operators in 60 countries with which Swiss Telecom has concluded roaming agreements.
U.S. TOPS FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENTS LIST

The United States heads the list of countries investing in India between August 1991 and December 1996. It garnered 26.63 percent of the total foreign direct investment (FDI) approvals of 956.75 billion rupees. The U.S. share in FDI approvals has increased every year from 1.85 billion rupees in 1991 to 100.56 billion in 1996.
EXPORT-ORIENTED UNITS MAY GET MORE OPERATIONAL FLEXIBILITY

The government is likely to allow greater operational flexibility to export-oriented units (EOUs) and export-processing zones (EPZs) in line with an expert panel's recommendations in the new export-import (Exim) policy for the next five years. Major recommendations include allowing EOUs, with orders for complementary products, to source from each other and export the items together. The panel also recommended giving sub-contracting permission through the eight-year period of the EOU's existence instead of on an yearly basis.
The Observer
BATA INDIA BACK IN THE BLACK

Shoe giant Bata India has announced a 41.5 million rupee profit for the year ended December 31, 1996. The company made a major recovery during the year since it had suffered a loss of 421.6 million rupees in the previous year. Bata's turnover rose to 5.9 billion rupees, an 11 percent increase over the previous year. The company did not declare a dividend.
ANOTHER ONE MLN TONNES OF WHEAT BEING IMPORTED

The State Trading Corporation (STC) has contracted import of another one million tonnes of Australian wheat, taking total import deals to 2.67 million tonnes. Though STC officials are silent about the deal, diplomatic circles confirmed the import for delivery in August, Sepember and December. Further imports were on the cards as STC had floated a global tender in the previous week. Though the tender was for import of 50,000 tonnes only, STC was known to have retained more in the past if the price was right.
COMMUNIST PARTY WANTS CHANGES IN BUDGET

The Communist Party of India (CPI) has demanded major modifications in the budget proposals. Their demands include a substantial increase in the allocation for the infrastructure sector, a 20 billion rupee increase for the power sector, and provision from the state coffers for wages, social security and housing for agricultural workers.
